Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 91:

﴿They said: "O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say."﴾ That is, we do not comprehend (ma nafqahu: "we do not understand"). ﴿Much of what you say﴾ such as the obligation of monotheism (tawhid) and the prohibition of diminishing (the measure, al-bakhs), and what you mentioned as evidence for them. This is due to the deficiency of their intellects and their failure to reflect. It has also been said that they spoke thus out of contempt for his speech, or because they did not give their minds to it, due to their intense aversion to it. ﴿And indeed we see you among us as weak.﴾ That is, you have no strength by which you could resist us if we intended you harm. Or (it means) "despised," having no honor. It has been said that it means "blind," in the dialect of Himyar; but apart from its lack of suitability, the restriction by the adverbial phrase (among us) rules this out. Some of the Mu'tazilah prohibited appointing a blind man as a prophet by analogy with judgeship and testimony, but the difference is clear. ﴿Were it not for your clan﴾ that is, your people, and their esteem in our sight because they follow our religion, not out of fear of their might. For the rahT (clan, rahṭ) is from three to ten, and it has been said up to nine. ﴿We would surely have stoned you﴾ that is, we would have killed you by pelting you with stones, or by the most grievous means. ﴿And you are not mighty against us﴾ so that your might would prevent us from stoning you. This is the practice of the foolish one who is confounded: he meets proofs and signs with abuse and threats. The placing of the pronoun after the negative particle (wa-ma anta 'alayna bi-'aziz, "you are not mighty against us") is a warning that the matter at issue is his (lack of might), not the affirmation of might, and that what restrains them from harming him is the might of his people, and for that reason.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 92–93:

﴿He said: "O my people, is my kinsfolk more esteemed by you than Allah? And you have taken Him behind your backs, cast away."﴾ And you made Him like the forgotten one, the cast-off, behind the back, by your associating others with Him and your insulting of His Messenger. So you do not spare me for the sake of Allah, yet you spare me for the sake of my kinsfolk. This (sentence) may carry the sense of denunciation, rebuke, rejection and denial. And ﴿ẓihriyyan﴾ (behind the back) is a relative noun derived from ẓahr (back), and the kasra (vowel) is one of the alterations of the relative form (nisba). ﴿Indeed my Lord is encompassing of what you do﴾, so nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for it.

﴿And, O my people, act according to your position; indeed I am acting. You will come to know who will receive a punishment that will disgrace him﴾. Its like has passed in the surah of al-An'am (al-An'am). The fa' in fa-﴿sawfa ta'lamun﴾ (then you will come to know) there is for the explicit statement that persistence and firm establishment in what they are upon is a cause of that. Its omission here is because it is the answer to a questioner who said: "Then what will happen after that?" So it is more emphatic in causing awe. ﴿And who is a liar﴾ is conjoined to "who will receive" (man ya'tihi), not because it is a counterpart to it, as in your saying: "You will know the liar and the truthful." Rather, because when they threatened him and called him a liar, he said: "You will come to know who is the one punished and who is the liar, between me and you." It was said that its analogous form would have been "and who is truthful," so that the first would refer to them and the second to him. But since they used to call him a liar, he said: "and who is a liar" according to their claim.

﴿And wait﴾, that is, await what I say to you. ﴿Indeed I am with you a watcher﴾, awaiting; (the form) fa'il here is in the sense of "one who watches" like ṣarīm, or "one who observes" like 'ashīr, or "one who is awaited" like rafī'.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 94–95:

﴿And when Our command came, We saved Shuʿayb and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us﴾. He mentioned it with the *wāw* (the conjunction "and"), as in the story of ʿĀd, since no promise had preceded it that would serve as a cause for it. This is unlike the stories of Ṣāliḥ and Lūṭ, for the destruction in those was mentioned after the promise, namely His saying: ﴿a promise not to be denied﴾, and His saying: ﴿Indeed, their appointed time is the morning﴾. Therefore it came with the *fāʾ* of causation (*fāʾ al-sababiyyah*, the *fāʾ* that indicates cause and consequence). ﴿And the cry seized those who did wrong﴾. It is said that Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him, cried out at them, and so they perished. ﴿So they became in their homes prostrate corpses﴾, meaning dead. The root of *al-judhūm* (prostrate, motionless) is *al-luzūm* (remaining in a place).

﴿As if they had never flourished therein﴾, meaning as if they had never dwelt there. ﴿Ah, away with Madyan, just as Thamūd was done away with﴾. He likened them to Thamūd because their punishment was likewise by the cry, except that the cry of Thamūd came from beneath them, while the cry of Madyan came from above them. It was also read *baʿudat* with a *ḍamma* (*baʿudat*), according to the original form, for the *kasra* (*baʿidat*) is a change made to restrict the meaning of *buʿd* (distance, being far) to what results from destruction. *Al-buʿd* is a verbal noun for both forms, while *al-baʿd* is the verbal noun of the form with *kasra*.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 96–97:

﴿And We certainly sent Musa with Our signs﴾ (meaning) with the Torah, or with the miracles. ﴿and a clear authority﴾, which is the overpowering miracles, or the staff. Its being singled out for mention is because it is the most dazzling of them. It is also permissible that both refer to one thing, i.e. "And We certainly sent him combining being Our signs and an authority for him in his prophethood, clear in itself or making it clear." For abāna (to make clear, to be clear) comes both intransitive (lāzim) and transitive (muta'addī). The difference between the two is that āya (sign) is general, covering any indicator and decisive proof, whereas sulṭān (authority) is restricted to the decisive, and mubīn (clear) is restricted to that which contains manifestness.

﴿to Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they followed the command of Pharaoh﴾ they followed his command in disbelieving in Musa, or rather they did not follow Musa, the guide to the truth, supported by the overpowering, dazzling miracles, and they followed the way of Pharaoh, who was immersed in error and transgression and who called to what its corruption does not conceal from anyone who has the least measure of intellect, because of the extreme ignorance of them and their lack of insight. ﴿And the command of Pharaoh was not right-guiding﴾, meaning not guiding (mursid) or possessing right guidance (dhū rushd); rather, it was pure misguidance (ghayy maḥḍ) and manifest error (ḍalāl ṣarīḥ).

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 98–99:

﴿He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection﴾ to the Fire, just as he used to lead them to misguidance in the world. It is said qadima (to go before) with the meaning of taqaddama (to go forward).

﴿So he will bring them down to the Fire﴾. He mentioned it in the past tense to emphasise its certainty, and he made the Fire for them into the position of water, so he called their arrival at it a mawrid (watering place). Then he said: ﴿And wretched is the watering place to which they are brought﴾, meaning: wretched is the watering place which they have come to. For water is sought to cool the livers and quench thirst, whereas the Fire is the opposite. The verse is like a proof for His saying: ﴿And the command of Pharaoh was not rightly guided﴾, for whoever has this as his end does not have rectitude in his affair. Or it is an explanation of it, on the basis that rashid (rightly guided) means that whose outcome is safe and praiseworthy.

﴿And they are followed in this world by a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning: they will be cursed in this world and in the Hereafter. ﴿Wretched is the gift that is given﴾, meaning: wretched is the help that is helped, or the gift that is given. Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 102–103:

﴿And thus﴾: like that seizing. ﴿is the seizing of your Lord﴾. It is also read as "akhadha rabbuka" (with the verb in the past tense), and on this reading the place of the kaf (ka, "like") is in the accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar). ﴿when He seizes the towns﴾: i.e., destroys them. It is also read "idh" because the meaning is in the past tense. ﴿while they are wrongdoing﴾: a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to "the towns", though in reality it belongs to their people; but since the towns were put in the place of their people, the description was applied to them. Its benefit is to indicate that they were seized because of their wrongdoing, and to warn every wrongdoer who wronged himself or others of the evil of the outcome. ﴿Indeed His seizing is painful, severe﴾: painful and grievous, from which there is no hoped-for escape. This is an intensification in threat and warning.

﴿Indeed in that﴾: i.e., in what befell the destroyed nations, or in what Allah the Exalted related of their stories. ﴿is surely a sign﴾: a lesson. ﴿for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter﴾: he takes lesson from it, recognising His greatness, knowing that what befell them is a model of what Allah has prepared for the criminals in the Hereafter; or he is restrained by it from its causes, knowing that it comes from a chooser-God who punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills. As for one who denies the Hereafter and holds that this world cannot end, he does not affirm a free, choosing agent, and attributes those events to astrological causes that happened to coincide in those days, not to the sins of those destroyed by them. ﴿That﴾: a reference to the Day of Resurrection and the punishment of the Hereafter, indicated by the context. ﴿is a Day on which mankind will be gathered﴾: i.e., mankind will be gathered for it. The change of form (to the passive participle) is to show the permanence of the meaning of gathering for the Day, and that it is inevitably part of its nature, and that people will not be free of it. This is more emphatic than His saying: ﴿the Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering﴾. The meaning of "gathered for it" is gathered for the reckoning and recompense that take place in it. ﴿And that is a Day witnessed﴾: i.e., a day in which the inhabitants of the heavens and earths are witnesses, so the verb is extended by treating the adverbial of time as an object, as in His statement: "in an assembly of the forelocks of men, witnessed," meaning many have witnessed it. Had the day itself been witnessed in its own right, the purpose of magnifying and distinguishing the day would be nullified, since all other days are likewise.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 104–105:

﴿And We do not delay it﴾, i.e., the Day. ﴿except for a limited term﴾, except until the expiry of a counted, finite period, with the noun (muḍāf, "term/period") elided, so that what is meant by "term" is the entire duration of the postponement, not its endpoint, for that endpoint is not counted.

﴿On the Day it comes﴾, i.e., the requital, or the Day, like His saying: ﴿Or until the Hour comes upon them﴾, on the basis that ﴿yawm﴾ (the Day) here means ḥīn (a time), or [it means] Allah, Mighty and Majestic, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do they await only that Allah should come to them in canopies of cloud﴾ and the like. Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read (yaʾti) with the elision of the yā' (final vowel letter), substituting for it the kasra (vowel). ﴿No soul will speak﴾, will not speak in a way that benefits or saves it, whether by an answer or by intercession. This is the governing element (nāṣib) of the time-adverb, and its accusative case may also be taken as governed by an implied verb "remember" (udhkur), or by the elided verb of "cessation" (al-intihāʾ).

﴿except by His permission﴾, except by the permission of Allah, like His saying: ﴿They will not speak except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted﴾, and this is in one station; and His saying: ﴿This is a Day on which they will not speak﴾ and ﴿nor will they be permitted, so they may make excuse﴾ belong to another station. Or, what is permitted is the true answers, and what is forbidden is the false excuses. ﴿Among them will be one who is wretched﴾, for whom the Fire has become obligatory by the requirement of the threat, ﴿and [another who is] happy﴾, for whom Paradise has become obligatory by the necessity of the promise. The pronoun refers to the people of the station, even though it is not mentioned, because it is known and indicated by His saying: ﴿No soul will speak﴾; or it refers to "mankind".

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 106–107:

﴿As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire, and therein for them will be sighing and wailing.﴾ Al-zafir (زَفِيرٌ) is the expulsion of breath, and al-shahiq (شَهِيقٌ) is its drawing back. Their use in the first and last part of the braying of a donkey (al-nahiq, نَهِيقٌ) is intended to indicate the intensity of their distress and grief, and to liken their state to one whose heart is overcome by heat and whose spirit is confined within it; or to liken their screaming to the voices of donkeys. It is also read (shuqu, شُقُوا) with a ḍammah.

﴿Abiding therein for as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾. It is not that the continuance of their abiding in the Fire is linked to the continuance of the heavens and the earth, for the texts indicate the perpetuity of their abiding and the cessation of the continuance of the heavens and the earth. Rather, the expression of perpetuity and emphasis is by means of what the Arabs used to express it, as a figure of speech. Had it been for linkage, it would not necessarily follow from the cessation of the heavens and the earth that their punishment ceases, nor from the continuance of the punishment that the heavens and the earth continue, except by way of implication (mafhum), since their continuance is like that which is implied by the continuance of the punishment; and you have learned that implication does not stand against explicit statement (mantuq). It has been said that what is meant is the heavens and earth of the Hereafter, and this is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens [as well]﴾, and that the people of the Hereafter must have some shade and some sustenance. But this is open to scrutiny, because it is a comparison with something that most of creation does not know to exist or to endure, and whoever knows it knows it only by what indicates the perpetuity of reward and punishment, so the comparison is of no benefit to him.

﴿Except what your Lord wills﴾. This is an exception from abiding in the Fire, because some of them, namely the sinful monotheists (fussaq al-muwahhidin), will come out of it. That suffices for the validity of the exception, because the removal of the ruling from the whole is satisfied by its removal from a part. They are the intended meaning of the second exception, for they are separated from Paradise during the days of their punishment. The perpetuity counted from a specified starting point is broken when considered from the beginning just as it is broken when considered from the end. And although these people became wretched through their disobedience, they became blessed through their faith. It should not be said that according to this, His saying ﴿Among them are the wretched and the blessed﴾ is not a valid division, because a condition of division is that the attribute of each part be absent from its counterpart; for that condition applies where the division is for real separation or where it prevents combination. Here, what is meant is that the people of the place of standing do not fall outside the two parts, and that their state is not free of happiness and wretchedness, and this does not prevent the two qualities from being combined in one person under two aspects. Or [the answer is] that the people of the Fire are sometimes moved from it to the Zamharir and other punishments, and likewise the people of Paradise are given bliss beyond Paradise, such as being joined to the presence of holiness and attaining the good pleasure of God and His meeting. Or the exception is from the ruling itself, and the excepted period is the time of their being held in the place of standing for reckoning, because the apparent sense requires that they be in the Fire at the time the Day comes. Or it is the period of their remaining in this world and the barzakh, if the ruling is taken as absolute and not restricted to the Day; and according to this interpretation, it is possible that the exception is from the abiding, as you have understood. It has been said that it is from His saying: ﴿For them therein is sighing and wailing﴾. It has also been said that illa here means "other than," as in your saying, "for a thousand, except the two old thousands," and the meaning is: other than what your Lord wills of additional duration without end beyond the lifespan of the heavens and the earth.

﴿Indeed, your Lord is the Accomplisher of what He intends﴾, without objection.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 109:

﴿So be not in doubt﴾ (about it), (i.e., in any) doubt, after what has been revealed to you concerning the final outcome of the people. ﴿Concerning what these worship﴾, (i.e., concerning the worship of) these polytheists, in that it is misguidance leading to the same fate that befell those before them, of whom I have related to you the evil end of their worship; or (it may refer to) the condition of what they worship, in that it harms and does not benefit. ﴿They worship only as their fathers worshipped before⁠﻿﻿ ﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿—﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿—﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿—﻿﻿ this is a resumptive clause whose meaning is to give the reason for the prohibition against doubt, i.e., they and their fathers are equal in polytheism. That is, they worship no worship except like the worship of their fathers, or they worship nothing except the same idols that their fathers worshipped. What befell their fathers of that has reached you, so the like of it will befall them, because similarity in causes necessitates similarity in effects. The meaning of ﴿as worshipped﴾ is "as they used to worship," and it is elided because of the indication of ﴿before﴾ referring to it. ﴿And indeed, We will pay them their share﴾, (i.e., their portion) of the punishment, like their fathers, or of the provision; in the latter case it constitutes an excuse for delaying the punishment from them despite the existence of what necessitates it.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 110–111:

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 112:

﴿So be steadfast as you have been commanded﴾ When He had explained the state of those who differ concerning monotheism (tawhid) and prophethood (nubuwwah), and had elaborated at length on the explanation of the promise and the threat, He commanded His Messenger ﷺ to be steadfast (istiqamah) just as he had been commanded. It encompasses steadfastness in beliefs, such as taking the middle course between anthropomorphism (tashbih) and negation of attributes (ta'til), so that the intellect remains preserved from both extremes; and steadfastness in actions, such as conveying the revelation and explaining the laws as they were sent down, and performing the duties of acts of worship without deficiency or excess that would cause the rights to be missed, and the like. This is in the utmost difficulty, and for this reason the prayer and peace of Allah be upon him said: "Hud has grayed me."

﴿And those who have repented with you﴾ That is, those who have repented from polytheism (shirk) and disbelief (kufr) and believed along with you. It is a conjunction with the pronoun hidden in "istaqim," and though it was not emphasized with a separate pronoun, the intervening element has taken its place. ﴿And do not transgress﴾ and do not go beyond what has been set as limits for you. ﴿Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do﴾ so He will recompense you for it; this carries the sense of giving a reason for the command and the prohibition. The verse is evidence for the obligation of following the texts without alteration or deviation through means such as analogy (qiyas) and juristic preference (istihsan).

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 113:

﴿And do not incline toward those who have done wrong﴾ — do not lean toward them even slightly, for al-rukun (inclination, leaning) is a slight inclination, such as dressing in their attire or glorifying their mention and continuing to do so. ﴿Lest the Fire touch you﴾ — because of your inclining toward them. If leaning toward one from whom something called wrongdoing has proceeded is like this, then what do you think of leaning toward the wrongdoers, i.e., those marked by wrongdoing, then inclining toward them entirely, then wrongdoing itself and immersion in it? Perhaps this verse is the most eloquent possible expression in forbidding wrongdoing and warning against it. The address to the Messenger (ﷺ) and those believers with him is for steadfastness in the uprightness which is justice, for departing from it by inclining to one of the two extremes, excess or deficiency, is wrongdoing against oneself or others, indeed wrongdoing against oneself itself. It has been recited as "tirkanu" and "fatimassakum" with a kasra on the ta' according to the dialect of Tamim, and as "turkanu" in the passive voice from arkanahu. ﴿And you have no protectors apart from Allah﴾ — no helpers who could prevent the punishment from you; the waw is for the circumstantial clause. ﴿Then you will not be helped﴾ — i.e., then Allah will not help you, since it has already been decreed in His judgment that He will punish you and not spare you. The "thumma" (then) here indicates the remoteness of His helping them, since He has threatened them with punishment for it and made it obligatory for them. It may also be that it is placed in the position of the "fa" (so) for the sense of remoteness, for when He explained that Allah is punishing them and that none other can help them, this produced the conclusion that they will not be helped at all.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 114–115:

﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾ — at dawn (ghudwah) and at dusk (ʿashiyyah). Its being in the accusative here is because it is in the position of an adverb of time (ẓarf), since it is governed by a noun (mudaf) that is joined to it. ﴿And at the approaches of the night﴾ — and hours of it near the day, for it comes from azlafahu, meaning "he brought it near," and zulaf is the plural of zulfah. The prayer of the morning (ghadāh) is the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ), because it is the prayer closest to the beginning of the day. The prayer of the evening (ʿashiyyah) is the afternoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr). It has also been said that it is the noon and afternoon prayers, because what comes after the decline of the sun (zawal) is considered evening. The prayer of the zulaf is the maghrib and ʿishāʾ prayers. It has been read as zulufan with two ḍammas, and with a ḍammah and a sukūn, like busr and bus̱r in busrah. And zulfā is in the sense of zulfah, like qurbā and qurbah. ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾ — they expiate them.

(And in a hadith: "Prayer from one prayer to the next is an expiation for what is between them, so long as the major sins are avoided." And regarding the occasion of revelation: "A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, 'I have had intercourse with a woman, except that I did not penetrate her,' and so this was revealed.")

﴿That﴾ is a reference to His saying ﴿so be upright﴾ and what follows it; it has also been said to refer to the Qur'an. ﴿A reminder for those who remember﴾ — an admonition for those who take heed.

﴿And be patient﴾ — in acts of obedience and in abstaining from sins. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the good-doers﴾ — this is a shift from the pronoun so that it serves as a proof for the intended meaning, and an indication that prayer and patience are ihsan (excellence), and an implicit signal that they are not counted without sincerity (ikhlas).

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 116–117:**

﴿So why were there not﴾, i.e. why did there not exist, ﴿among the generations before you, people of remainder﴾, i.e. of judgment and intellect, ﴿or people of excellence?﴾ The word ﴿remainder﴾ (baqiyyah) is used because a man preserves the best of what he produces, and from this one says, "So-and-so is from the remainder of the people," meaning from their best. It is also permissible for it to be a verbal noun (maṣdar) like taqiyyah (guarding oneself), meaning people who guard themselves and protect themselves from punishment. This is supported by the fact that it was read as baqyah, which is the single instance from the verbal noun of baqāhu, yubqīhi, when he watched over him. ﴿Who forbade corruption in the earth, except a few of those whom We saved from them.﴾ But a few of them We saved, because they were like that. Its connection [to what precedes] is not valid unless it is made an exception (istithnā', exception) from the necessary negation implied by the tahḍīḍ (exhortative urging). ﴿And those who did wrong followed what they were made to enjoy in it.﴾ What they were given of desires, were preoccupied with obtaining their causes, and turned away from what lies beyond that. ﴿And they were criminals﴾, i.e. disbelievers. It is as if He intended to explain what was the cause of the annihilation of the earlier nations, namely the spread of wrongdoing among them, their following of desire, and their abandonment of forbidding evil deeds together with disbelief. His saying ﴿and followed﴾ is in the sense of a implied conjunction (ma'ṭūf muḍmar) which the speech indicates, since the meaning is: they did not forbid corruption, and those who did wrong followed, and they were criminals. It is conjoined to (ittaba'a), or it is interposed. It was also read as wa-atba'a, meaning and they followed the reward of what they were made to enjoy, so the wāw is for the ḥāl (circumstantial clause). It is also permissible to interpret the well-known reading in this way, and the preceding mention of salvation supports it.

﴿And your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly﴾, i.e. through shirk (association of partners with God). ﴿While their people are reformers﴾ among themselves, not adding to their shirk corruption and mutual oppression. This is due to the abundance of His mercy and His leniency regarding His rights. From this, the jurists gave precedence, when rights conflict, to the rights of people (ḥuqūq al-'ibād, the rights of human beings). It has been said: sovereignty (al-mulk) remains with shirk, but does not remain with injustice.
